rule: good. the rule line is never parsed, so it needs no rewrite; the work for this item is in the first and third sentences.
texts: bad: 'leaves a lantern untended overnight' packs a state, a duplicate flat copy of that state and a result link into the rule's trigger, so the condition only fires on a knowledge base that already holds all of them, and the dying that comes out is keyed to the lantern rather than to that night, so two untended nights for one lantern merge into a single dying. Since 'leaves ... untended' names no event of its own, state the condition as a plain state clause with the Keeper as possessor: "When a Keeper's lantern is untended all night, the lantern dies before dawn."

good. the plain state condition plus a plain consequent gives a fireable rule that was adjudicated faithful; the only thing not carried is the whole-night extent of 'through the night', which lands as a plain night-time slot.

bad: 'the mire-essence' comes out as the bare kind word rather than as a specific portion — while 'the wick' in the same clause does get its own referent — so the two definites are stored inconsistently and a question about one lantern's essence will not match; 'during the night' also has no supported frame relation and survives only as a plain night slot. Rewrite as: "A Keeper refreshes a lantern's mire-essence and trims its wick at night."
